records.title: Defining openness as traceable research infrastructure
records.analytic_role: One grounded-theory incident developed from four exact interview passages.

method_payload.open_code: Defining openness as traceable research infrastructure
method_payload.meaning: Open Science is understood as making results, procedures, data, code, and decisions available so others can retrace and evaluate the research.

anchors.selected_text: Well, there's several several aspects to this, right? Open accessibility of results, right? Sort of open access, that whole topic, which I'm sure we'll talk about in more depth as the interview continues. Availability of procedures, data, anything basically that ensures reproducibility of study designs, replicability ideally, and we've talked about this outside of this interview already quite a bit. So basically it's at an ideal plane, it's making available everything that goes into the research that enables basically anybody in the world to trace the steps of that research, arrive at the same results, and also critically evaluate each and every individual step.

anchors.selected_text: For me, open science is being rigorous about your whole research process from the planning stage through the actual research, through the publication stage. And it's, I guess for me, not only about making everything publicly available, but also making my own life easier because it entails like writing very rigorous documentation in the sense of documenting decisions I made, say, in corpus linguistic when it comes to annotation, which, yeah, part of my data did I annotate? How and why, what were the critical parts that we discussed in the team. So it's about making it reusable for others, but also reusable for me later.

records.title: Directory constitutional design as diagnostic evidence
records.analytic_role: One process-tracing evidence item retained for causal diagnostic testing.

anchors.selected_text: Its constitutional design tried to avoid both one-man tyranny and uncontrolled democratic radicalism.
anchors.context_text:
1795: The Directory replaced the Thermidorian Convention. Source D says the new
regime was built around a five-member executive, the Council of Ancients, and
the Council of Five Hundred. Its constitutional design tried to avoid both
one-man tyranny and uncontrolled democratic radicalism.

interpretation_boundary: The same anchor contract preserves source identity for both methods; grounded-theory incident meaning and process-tracing diagnostic metadata remain separate and are never collapsed into a shared evidence score.
non_claims: This view does not adopt a shared Data Contracts schema.
This view does not claim that grounded theory and process tracing use evidence identically.
This view does not convert qualitative support into causal diagnostic weight.
The inspected revisions identify artifacts reviewed; neither source artifact records its own producer Git revision.
